clue.text: Pancake roll — it surprisingly fills group of volunteers

indicators.note: fills says the scrambled letters go inside the volunteers' abbreviation

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: surprisingly says the letters of roll and it come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A food item called a pancake roll is unexpectedly being served to a band of volunteers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pancake roll' reads as one dish, but only 'Pancake' defines; 'roll' joins 'it' as fodder. 'surprisingly' turns ROLLIT into ORTILL, which 'fills' TA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican flatbread of maize or wheat is thin and round, much like a griddled batter disc.

parts.note: a jar is a common container for jam or pickles

explanation.surface: Something is slightly open, namely a box or tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left slightly open is said to stand thus, a standard synonym.

indicators.note: reportedly says we hear the word rather than see it spelt, so take the sound alone

parts.note: coarser means grosser, ruder or more vulgar

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper is said to be rather vulgar.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of food and household goods runs a shop, so is a type of shopkeeper.

clue.text: Nato needs reorganising? Agree no end, but don't mention it

indicators.note: needs reorganising tells us the four letters of Nato must be rearranged
no end says the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to agree is to tally, as figures that match

explanation.surface: A political comment: NATO must be restructured, so concede the point but keep quiet about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs reorganising' turns NATO into NOTA; 'no end' trims TALLY (agree) to TALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A polite reply to thanks, meaning the favour was no trouble, like saying you're welcome.

clue.text: Refuse to walk with primate in conflict

indicators.note: in says the walk and primate pieces sit inside the conflict word

parts.note: a war is an armed conflict
to step is to walk
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: Someone declines to go for a stroll with a monkey during wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb (decline) but is the noun, rubbish; 'in' puts the walk and the primate inside the conflict word.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded office paper is a kind of rubbish, so it is refuse in the noun sense.

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the word fed is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an end is a boundary or edge, a border

explanation.surface: A sentry stationed on a frontier who is sick of the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed up' reads as one phrase meaning bored, but 'up' is the reversal signal, giving DEF.
explanation.definitionFit: To protect something from attack is to shield it, a straightforward synonym.

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
a juror sits on a jury, a panel of twelve

explanation.surface: A member of a review panel turns out to be a magician.
explanation.walkthrough: CON for study is an old literary sense, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer of tricks and illusions is a magician, also spelled conjurer.

indicators.note: surrounding says the others word wraps around the island abbreviation

parts.note: the rest means the others, those remaining
Is is the standard abbreviation for island, as on maps

explanation.surface: Other people encircle an island to stand against it.
explanation.definitionFit: To withstand or fight against something is to oppose it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Ring about backing for Roger, a playwright

parts.note: a ring is O-shaped
ca is short for circa, about

indicators.note: backing says the word is read in reverse

parts.note: Roger is radio talk for yes, message received

explanation.surface: Someone telephones about support for a man named Roger, who writes plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests a phone call; it is O. 'backing' turns YES (Roger in radio talk) into SEY. Sean O'Casey was an Irish dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Sean O'Casey was an Irish dramatist, author of Juno and the Paycock.

indicators.note: half says take only the front half of the word's letters

parts.note: starkers is British slang for naked

explanation.surface: A famous person caught partly undressed.
explanation.walkthrough: STARKERS is British slang for stark naked; its first half gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous performer or personality is a celebrity, a common synonym.

parts.note: casual relationships are uncommitted or promiscuous ones
ties are connections or relationships

explanation.surface: People suffer from loose sexual liaisons.
explanation.definitionFit: Those injured or killed in an accident or battle are its victims.

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
to lower something is to put it down

explanation.surface: A clergyman hangs up the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blower' is British slang for the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang names the phone after the speaking tube one would blow into.

clue.text: Stagecoach company provides for writer with a long way to travel

parts.note: H G Wells was the English author of The Time Machine
far means a long way
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A coach operator caters for an author facing a long journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stagecoach' could suggest the British bus firm; here it is the Wild West firm. H G Wells is the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The American firm ran horse-drawn mail and passenger services across the West before becoming a bank.

parts.note: to impress a mark is to stamp it

indicators.note: leader points to the first letter of Estonia

explanation.surface: A political figure from Estonia made a good impression during a trip abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests an air trip; here it is a panicked rush. STAMPED (impressed) plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass panicked rush of animals or people is a headlong flight from danger.

clue.text: In the end, book of maps is printed on time

parts.note: an atlas is a bound book of maps
T is the abbreviation for time, as in physics

explanation.surface: Eventually an atlas is published on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean finally, after a long wait.

clue.text: Fellow crew member — he maps it at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor plots the course for the rest of the voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who serves on the same vessel as you is your companion aboard, a fellow sailor.

indicators.note: rotating suggests turning the word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: pupils are school students

explanation.surface: A teacher errs by moving the class around.
explanation.definitionFit: To blunder or err is to commit an error, the verb phrase used informally.

clue.text: Reserve wanting place on a team

parts.note: to put something is to place it
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A substitute player longing to get into a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' reads as a noun (a substitute player) but is the verb, set apart for later.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something back for later use is to save or reserve it.

clue.text: New zebra crossing good in capital

indicators.note: crossing says the rearranged animal goes across, around, the good abbreviation
new says the letters of zebra are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A newly painted pedestrian crossing in good condition in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zebra crossing' is the British name for a striped pedestrian crossing; here 'New' turns ZEBRA into ZABRE and 'crossing' puts it round G.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the seat of government of Croatia, its capital.

clue.text: Unfaithful woman is sad, cries out

indicators.note: out says the letters are disordered or set out afresh

explanation.surface: A betrayed lover weeps, overcome with sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: Cressida, in Chaucer and Shakespeare, deserts Troilus for Diomedes.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Troy legend she betrays her lover Troilus, a byword for faithlessness.

explanation.surface: An alphabet book for children: J stands for jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: J is drug slang short for joint, a cannabis cigarette; a reefer jacket is a short double-breasted coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both slang for a cannabis cigarette (a joint, J) and a sailor's thick double-breasted coat.

clue.text: Plagiarist gets head of publishing very annoyed

indicators.note: head of points to the first letter of publishing

parts.note: irate means very angry or annoyed

explanation.surface: A copier of others' work infuriates the boss of a publishing house.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who copies or reproduces others' work without permission is a literary thief.

indicators.note: around says the location word wraps round the letter a

parts.note: a place is a location

explanation.surface: The place surrounding the home of a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckingham is the classic example of a monarch's official home.

clue.text: See butterfly in real Madrid ground?

indicators.note: ground means crushed or pulverised, so the letters are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: Spot an insect flitting about the Real Madrid football stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' suggests a football stadium but signals the anagram, as in ground coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A common European species with black wings banded in red, a kind of butterfly.

explanation.surface: Prize money awarded to a tennis champion.
explanation.walkthrough: Pat Cash, the Australian, won the Wimbledon men's singles in 1987.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means ready money, notes and coins, and is the surname of 1987 Wimbledon champion Pat.

clue.text: Bag, an essential in emergency stop?

indicators.note: essential in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bag is something every driver needs for a sudden halt, an airbag perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy a sac or pouch of fluid in the body is a small bag.

parts.note: an eight is a racing boat crew of eight rowers

explanation.surface: A western rowing team holds sway.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry weight is to have sway or importance, so the noun means influence.

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A fan backing the club from the back of the stands.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttocks are the rear end, a colloquial synonym.
